# ChatGPT Voice

<!-- vimeo: 1216145640 | track: English (auto-generated) -->

<details>
<summary>자막: ChatGPT Voice</summary>

Sometimes the fastest way to develop an idea is to talk it through. ChatGPT Voice lets you have a spoken conversation with ChatGPT, hear the response, interrupt naturally, and continue working in the same chat. Begin in your agency's authorized ChatGPT workspace. Select the voice control in the prompt area and allow microphone access when prompted. In eligible accounts, Voice can also be used with work in the ChatGPT desktop app. Availability and controls may depend on your plan, workspace settings, and app version. Here's a practical example. A fictional federal program analyst is preparing for a leadership review but has only rough notes. Instead of trying to write the perfect prompt, the employee says, "I am preparing for a program review. Ask me five questions, one at a time, to help me identify the decision leadership needs to make. Challenge unclear assumptions and ask what information is missing." ChatGPT asks a question, listens to the answer, and continues the conversation. The employee can interrupt, correct an assumption, add context, or ask for a different question. This conversational format can make it easier to discover gaps, rehearse an explanation, and organize ideas before drafting a formal product. When the discussion is complete, the employee says, "Summarize my answers into three briefing points, two open questions, and one recommended next step. Separate verified facts from assumptions." The resulting text remains in the chat where the employee can review it, edit it, and continue working. Voice reduces the friction of getting started, but it does not replace judgment. Use only information authorized for your workspace. Be mindful of who can hear you, and verify important facts, dates, numbers, and recommendations before you brief, send, or act.
